title: Difference between Each and Every (Pronoun vs Adjective)
formula: Each (Pronoun / Adjective for 2 or more) | Every (Strictly Adjective for > 2) + Singular Noun + Singular Verb
ruleDescription:
**'Each' vs 'Every' Core Distinctions:**
1. **Each** refers to two or more individual members. It can function as both a **Pronoun** ('Each of the boys') and an **Adjective** ('Each boy').
2. **Every** refers to more than two members collectively. It functions **ONLY as an Adjective** ('Every boy'). It CANNOT function as a pronoun (e.g., 'Every of the boys' ❌ is completely wrong).
3. Both always take a **Singular Countable Noun** and a **Singular Verb**.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Each' और 'Every' दोनों के साथ हमेशा Singular Noun और Singular Verb आता है।
**महत्वपूर्ण अंतर**:
• **Each**: दो या दो से अधिक के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है। यह Pronoun ('Each of the students') और Adjective ('Each student') दोनों बनता है।
• **Every**: केवल दो से अधिक के लिए आता है। यह केवल Adjective होता है ('Every of...' ❌ कभी नहीं होता)।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Each of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb` | `Each / Every + Singular Noun + Singular Verb`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Every of my friends is ready' ❌ गलत है; 'Each of my friends is ready' ✔ सही है।

correctExample: Each of my friends is ready.

title: Both and Not Cannot Be Used Together (Use Neither... Nor)
formula: Both + And (Positive Pairs only) | Neither... Nor (For Negative Pairs of Two)
ruleDescription:
**'Both' & 'Neither' Core Rules:**
1. **'Both'** is never used in negative sentences with 'not'. When expressing that neither of two things is true, use **'Neither... nor'**.
2. **'Both'** is always paired with **'and'** (never with 'as well as' or 'along with').
3. 'Neither' is used exclusively for two persons/things. For more than two, use **'None'**.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Both' का प्रयोग कभी भी 'Not' के साथ नकारात्मक वाक्यों में नहीं होता। दो में से किसी के भी न होने पर **'Neither... nor'** का प्रयोग करें।
**नियम व जोड़े**:
• 'Both... and' हमेशा सकारात्मक जोड़े के लिए आता है (Both Ram and Shyam).
• 'Both of them did not come' ❌ गलत है; 'Neither of them came' ✔ सही है।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Neither of + Plural Noun (Two items) + Singular Verb`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Both Ram as well as Shyam' ❌ गलत है; 'Both Ram and Shyam' ✔ सही है।

title: Usage of Relative Pronouns: Who, Whom, Which, That
formula: Who (Subject Person) | Whom (Object Person) | Which (Things/Animals) | That (Superlatives, All, Same, Only, None)
ruleDescription:
**Relative Pronouns Exhaustive Usage:**
1. **Who**: Used as a Subject for persons ('The doctor who treated me').
2. **Whom**: Used as an Object for persons ('The man whom I met').
3. **Which**: Used for non-living things, animals, and making a choice among many ('Which of the two pens do you want?').
4. **That**: Strictly mandatory instead of 'which/who' after:
• Superlative Degrees (The best, The greatest)
• Indefinite words: `All`, `Same`, `Only`, `None`, `Nothing`, `Little`, `Few`, `Any`
• Pairs of living person + animal/thing ('The man and his dog that were walking').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Relative Pronouns का सही चयन:
• **Who**: कर्ता (Subject) के लिए आता है (क्रिया से ठीक पहले)।
• **Whom**: कर्म (Object) के लिए आता है।
• **Which**: निर्जीव वस्तुओं और जानवरों के लिए आता है।
• **That** का अनिवार्य प्रयोग: Superlative degree ('the best that'), All, Same, Only, None, Nothing, Little, Few के बाद हमेशा **'That'** आता है ('Which' ❌ नहीं)।
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'All which glitters is not gold' ❌ गलत है; 'All that glitters is not gold' ✔ सही है।

title: Three Types of Conditional Sentences (Types 0, 1, 2, 3)
formula: Conditional Sentences: Type 1 (If + V₁ ➔ Will + V₁) | Type 2 (If + V₂/Were ➔ Would + V₁) | Type 3 (If + Had + V₃ ➔ Would have + V₃)
ruleDescription:
**Master Conditional Structure Table:**
1. **Zero Conditional (Universal Truths)**: `If + Simple Present ➔ Simple Present`
2. **First Conditional (Real/Future Possibility)**: `If + Simple Present (V₁/V₅) ➔ Will / Shall / Can / May + V₁`
3. **Second Conditional (Unreal Present/Hypothetical)**: `If + Simple Past (V₂ / Were) ➔ Would / Could / Might + V₁`
4. **Third Conditional (Unfulfilled Past Action)**: `If + Past Perfect (Had + V₃) ➔ Would have / Could have + V₃`
**Golden Rule**: Never use 'will/would/shall' inside the 'If-clause' (e.g., 'If it will rain' ➔ 'If it rains' ).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Conditional Sentences के 3 मुख्य प्रकार:
**Type 1**: `If + Simple Present (V₁/V₅) ➔ Will + V₁` (यदि तुम पढ़ोगे तो पास होगे - If you study, you will pass).
**Type 2**: `If + Simple Past (V₂/Were) ➔ Would + V₁` (काल्पनिक वर्तमान - If I had money, I would help you).
**Type 3**: `If + Had + V₃ ➔ Would have + V₃` (अतीत की अपूर्ण शर्त - If you had worked hard, you would have passed).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'If clause' में कभी भी 'will/shall/would' का प्रयोग न करें।

correctExample: If he had worked hard, he would have passed.

title: One of the + Plural Noun + Singular Verb vs Relative Pronoun
formula: One of the + Plural Noun + Singular Verb | One of the + Plural Noun + Relative Pronoun (Who/That) + Plural Verb | Only one of the... + Singular Verb
ruleDescription:
**The 'One of the' Rule Matrix:**
1. **Standard Form**: When 'One of the' is the Subject, the noun is plural, but the verb is singular:
• `One of the students is absent today.`
2. **With Relative Pronoun (Who/That/Which)**: The verb agrees with the plural antecedent immediately before the relative pronoun:
• `He is one of the players who have won the match.`
3. **With 'Only one of the'**: The focus returns exclusively to 'only one', so the verb is singular:
• `This is the only one of his novels that is worth reading.`
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'One of the' का 3-स्तरीय नियम:
**1. साधारण नियम**: `One of the + Plural Noun + Singular Verb` (e.g. One of my friends is a doctor).
**2. Relative Pronoun (Who/That) होने पर**: Verb अपने ठीक पहले वाले Plural Noun के अनुसार **Plural** होगी (e.g. He is one of the men who have helped me).
**3. 'Only one of the' होने पर**: Verb हमेशा **Singular** होगी (e.g. He is the only one of the boys who has scored 100).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'One of the boy' ❌ कभी नहीं होता; हमेशा 'One of the boys' ✔ होता है।

title: Hyphenated Compound Adjectives (Number + Unit + Noun)

ruleDescription:
When a combination of **'Number + Unit + Noun'** or **'Number + Unit + Adjective'** functions as a compound modifier before a noun, the unit must strictly be in the **Singular Form** (never plural with 's'):
**Exhaustive List of Compound Modifiers:**
• `A ten-rupee note` (NOT 'A ten-rupees note' ❌)
• `A five-star hotel` (NOT 'A five-stars hotel' ❌)
• `A three-hour exam` (NOT 'A three-hours exam' ❌)
• `A two-mile walk` (NOT 'A two-miles walk' ❌)
• `A five-year plan` (NOT 'A five-years plan' ❌)
• `A six-man committee` (NOT 'A six-men committee' ❌)
• `A four-foot ruler` (NOT 'A four-feet ruler' ❌).
**Contrast**: If no noun follows the unit, it takes the plural form: 'He gave me ten rupees' ✔.

title: Plural Nouns Expressing Quantity, Distance, Money as Single Unit
formula: Plural Noun of Definite Quantity / Distance / Money / Time + SINGULAR VERB (When thought of as a single whole)
ruleDescription:
When a plural noun denotes a specific **quantity, distance, amount of money, weight, or period of time** considered as a single collective unit, it takes a **Singular Verb**:
**Key Measurement Units:**
• **Distance**: `Ten miles is a long distance to walk.`
• **Money**: `Fifty thousand rupees is a handsome amount.`
• **Time**: `Five years is the maximum term for this post.`
• **Weight**: `Ten tons of wheat was imported.`
**Exception (When Divided / Individual Units)**: If the amount is spent separately or individual units are considered, use a **Plural Verb**:
• 'Fifty thousand rupees were distributed among the victims' ✔.

**मुख्य नियम**: जब कोई Plural Noun किसी निश्चित दूरी (Distance), राशि (Money), समय (Time) या भार (Weight) को एक इकाई (Single Unit) के रूप में दर्शाता है, तो **Singular Verb** आती है।
**प्रमुख उदाहरण**:
• Ten kilometers **is** a long walk.
• Fifty thousand rupees **is** a huge sum.
• Three hours **is** sufficient for the test.
**अपवाद**: यदि राशि अलग-अलग खर्च की जाए या विभाजित हो, तो Plural Verb आएगी (जैसे 'Five hundred rupees were spent on books and clothes').

title: Latin Adjectives Taking 'To' Instead of 'Than' (Senior, Junior, Superior)
formula: Latin Comparative (Senior/Junior/Superior/Inferior/Prior/Anterior/Posterior/Preferable) + TO [Never 'Than' or 'More/Most']
ruleDescription:
The following Latin adjectives always end in **'-ior'** and take the preposition **'to'** instead of 'than'. They are already comparative in nature, so they NEVER take 'more' or 'most':
**Complete List of Latin Adjectives:**
1. **Senior** (senior to)
2. **Junior** (junior to)
3. **Superior** (superior to)
4. **Inferior** (inferior to)
5. **Prior** (prior to)
6. **Anterior** (anterior to)
7. **Posterior** (posterior to)
8. **Preferable** (preferable to)
9. **Elder** (elder to).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: वे Latin Adjectives जो '-ior' पर समाप्त होते हैं, उनके बाद कभी भी 'than' या 'more/most' नहीं आता; हमेशा Preposition **'to'** का प्रयोग होता है।
**पूरी सूची**: Senior, Junior, Superior, Inferior, Prior, Anterior, Posterior, Preferable, Elder.
**फॉर्मूला**: `Subject + Verb + [Latin Adjective] + TO + Object`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He is more senior than me' ❌ गलत है; सही वाक्य 'He is senior to me' ✔ होगा।

title: Law of Inversion with Hardly, Scarcely Followed by 'When'
formula: Hardly / Scarcely + Had + Subject + V₃ + WHEN (or Before) [Never 'Than' or 'Then']
ruleDescription:
**Inversion with Hardly & Scarcely:**
1. When **Hardly** or **Scarcely** begins a sentence, the **Law of Inversion** applies (Auxiliary verb precedes Subject).
2. They are strictly paired with **'WHEN'** (or occasionally 'before'), NEVER with 'than' or 'then'.
3. Structures:
• `Hardly + had + Subject + V₃ + when + Subject + V₂`
• `Hardly + did + Subject + V₁ + when + Subject + V₂`
4. Being negative adverbs, do NOT use 'not' in the hardly/scarcely clause.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब वाक्य 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' से शुरू हो, तो:
1. **Inversion** होता है (Helping Verb कर्ता से पहले आती है)।
2. इनका जोड़ा हमेशा **'WHEN'** (या before) के साथ बनता है ('Than' ❌ या 'Then' ❌ कभी नहीं आता)।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Hardly / Scarcely + had + Sub + V₃ + WHEN + Sub + V₂`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Hardly had I arrived than it began to rain' ❌ गलत है; 'Hardly had I arrived when it began to rain' ✔ सही है।

title: Sequence of Past Actions (Past Perfect vs Simple Past with Before/After)
formula: First Completed Action (Past Perfect: Had + V₃) + Before / After + Second Action (Simple Past: V₂)
ruleDescription:
When two actions happened in the past, one after another:
1. The **First / Earlier Action** must strictly be in the **Past Perfect Tense (Had + V₃)**.
2. The **Second / Later Action** must be in the **Simple Past Tense (V₂)**.
**Key Time Conjunctions:**
• `[Had + V₃] + BEFORE + [V₂]` ➔ *The patient had died before the doctor arrived.*
• `[V₂] + AFTER + [Had + V₃]` ➔ *The train started after I had bought the ticket.*
• `As soon as / By the time` ➔ *By the time the police came, the thief had fled.*
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: भूतकाल (Past) में एक के बाद एक हुए दो कार्यों में:
**1. पहले समाप्त हुआ कार्य**: `Past Perfect (Had + V₃)`
**2. बाद में हुआ कार्य**: `Simple Past (V₂)`
**प्रमुख संरचनाएं**:
• `Had + V₃ + BEFORE + V₂` (डॉक्टर के आने से पहले रोगी मर चुका था - The patient had died before the doctor came).
• `V₂ + AFTER + Had + V₃` (मेरे टिकट लेने के बाद ट्रेन चली - The train departed after I had bought the ticket).
**परीक्षा टिप**: दोनों भागों में कभी भी 'had + V₃' या दोनों में 'V₂' एक साथ न लगाएं।

title: Possessive Adjective Before a Gerund (V-ing)
formula: Possessive Adjective (My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their, Ram's) + GERUND (V-ing) [Never Objective Pronoun]
ruleDescription:
A **Gerund** is a verb ending in '-ing' functioning as a noun. Whenever a noun or pronoun precedes a gerund, it must be in the **Possessive Case** (my, your, his, her, their, our, noun's), NEVER in the Objective Case (me, him, them, us, you):
**Key Pronoun Transformations Before Gerund:**
• `Me going` ➔ **My going** ✔
• `Him arriving late` ➔ **His arriving late** ✔
• `Them shouting` ➔ **Their shouting** ✔
• `Us speaking` ➔ **Our speaking** ✔
• `Ram coming` ➔ **Ram's coming** ✔.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Gerund (Verb + ing जो संज्ञा का कार्य करे) से ठीक पहले आने वाला Pronoun या Noun हमेशा **Possessive Case** (My, Your, His, Her, Their, Our, Ram's) में होता है (Objective Case में नहीं)।
**सही व गलत रूप**:
• 'I don't like **him** coming late' ❌ ➔ 'I don't like **his** coming late' ✔
• 'He insisted on **me** going' ❌ ➔ 'He insisted on **my** going' ✔
• 'She objected to **them** shouting' ❌ ➔ 'She objected to **their** shouting' ✔.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He was confident of him passing' ❌ गलत है; 'of his passing' ✔ सही है।

title: Law of Inversion with No Sooner... Than
formula: No Sooner + Had / Did + Subject + V₃ / V₁ + THAN + Subject + V₂ [Never 'When', 'Then', 'That']
ruleDescription:
**Law of Inversion with 'No Sooner... Than':**
1. When **No Sooner** starts a sentence, inversion takes place.
2. **'No sooner'** is correlatively paired strictly with **'THAN'** (T-H-A-N), never with 'when', 'then', or 'that'.
3. Structures:
• `No sooner + had + Subject + V₃ + THAN + Subject + V₂`
• `No sooner + did + Subject + V₁ + THAN + Subject + V₂`.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'No sooner' का नियम:
1. वाक्य के प्रारंभ में आने पर **Inversion** (Had/Did + Subject) होता है।
2. इसका जोड़ा हमेशा **'THAN'** (T-H-A-N) होता है ('When' ❌ या 'Then' ❌ नहीं)।
**फॉर्मूला**: `No sooner + had + Sub + V₃ + THAN + Sub + V₂`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'No sooner did I see the tiger when I ran away' ❌ गलत है; सही 'No sooner did I see the tiger than I ran away' ✔ होगा।

title: Articles with Two Nouns Joined by 'And' (Single vs Dual Identity)
formula: The + Noun₁ + and + Noun₂ (Single Person/Thing ➔ Singular Verb) | The + Noun₁ + and + The + Noun₂ (Two Different Persons/Things ➔ Plural Verb)
ruleDescription:
**Article Count Determines Subject Number:**
1. **Single Article (One Person/Unit)**: If the article ('The' / 'A') is used before only the first noun, both nouns refer to the same single person or idea ➔ Takes **Singular Verb**:
• `The Director and Producer is coming.` (Same person is director & producer).
2. **Double Article (Two Separate Persons/Units)**: If the article is repeated before both nouns, they refer to two distinct individuals ➔ Takes **Plural Verb**:
• `The Director and The Producer are coming.` (Two different individuals).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Article 'The/A' की संख्या से Subject का Singular या Plural होना तय होता है:
**1. केवल पहले Noun के साथ Article**: दोनों Nouns एक ही व्यक्ति या पद को दर्शाते हैं ➔ **Singular Verb** (e.g. The poet and scholar **is** dead).
**2. दोनों Nouns के साथ Article**: दोनों Nouns अलग-अलग व्यक्तियों को दर्शाते हैं ➔ **Plural Verb** (e.g. The poet and the scholar **are** dead).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'A black and white cow are grazing' (एक ही गाय जो काली-सफेद है ➔ is grazing होगा)।

title: Preposition 'To' Followed by Gerund (Looking forward to, Used to + V-ing)
formula: Specific Verb/Phrase + TO + Gerund (V-ing) [Looking forward to, Used to, Accustomed to, With a view to + V-ing]
ruleDescription:
Normally 'to' is followed by V₁ (Infinitive), but when 'to' is part of specific fixed prepositional phrases, it is followed by a **Gerund (V-ing)**:
**Exhaustive List of 'To + Gerund' Phrases:**
1. **Looking forward to** (looking forward to meeting)
2. **Be / Get used to** (used to waking up early)
3. **Accustomed to** (accustomed to working late)
4. **With a view to** (with a view to helping)
5. **Addicted to** (addicted to gambling)
6. **Devoted to** (devoted to serving)
7. **Habituated to** (habituated to drinking)
8. **In addition to** (in addition to teaching)
9. **Object to / Opposed to** (objected to paying)
10. **Prone to / Averse to** (prone to making errors)
11. **Given to / Taken to** (taken to smoking)
12. **Confess to** (confessed to stealing).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: सामान्यतः 'To' के बाद V₁ आता है, लेकिन इन विशेष Phrasal Prepositions में 'To' के बाद हमेशा **Gerund (Verb + ing)** आता है।
**पूरी सूची**: Looking forward to, With a view to, Be used to, Accustomed to, Addicted to, Devoted to, Habituated to, In addition to, Object to, Prone to, Averse to, Taken to.
**फॉर्मूला**: `Subject + [Phrase] + TO + Verb-ing`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'I am looking forward to meet you' ❌ गलत है; 'I am looking forward to meeting you' ✔ सही है।

title: Verbs Requiring Reflexive Pronouns (Avail, Adapt, Reconcile, Enjoy)
formula: Reflexive Verb + Reflexive Pronoun (Myself, Himself, Themselves, Herself) [When Transitive without Object]
ruleDescription:
Certain verbs always require a **Reflexive Pronoun** (myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves, themselves) when they are not followed by a direct object:
**Verbs Requiring Reflexive Pronouns:**
1. **Avail** (avail oneself of)
2. **Adapt / Adjust** (adapt himself to)
3. **Acquit** (acquit oneself well)
4. **Absent** (absented himself from)
5. **Reconcile** (reconcile oneself to)
6. **Amuse** (amused themselves)
7. **Resign** (resigned himself to fate)
8. **Avenge / Revenge** (avenged himself)
9. **Exert / Apply** (exert yourself)
10. **Pride** (prides herself on)
11. **Enjoy / Introduce** (enjoyed themselves at the party).
**Verbs that NEVER Take Reflexive Pronouns:**
`Keep`, `Break`, `Feed`, `Hide`, `Burst`, `Stop`, `Turn`, `Qualify`, `Bathe`, `Move`, `Rest`.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: यदि इन क्रियाओं के बाद कोई Direct Object न हो, तो इनके साथ Reflexive Pronoun (himself, myself, themselves) लगाना अनिवार्य है।
**Reflexive लेने वाली Verbs**: Avail (of), Adapt, Acquit, Absent, Reconcile, Amuse, Resign, Avenge, Exert, Apply, Pride (on), Enjoy.
**Reflexive कभी न लेने वाली Verbs**: Keep, Stop, Turn, Qualify, Bathe, Move, Rest, Hide.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He absented from class yesterday' ❌ गलत है; 'He absented himself from class yesterday' ✔ सही है।

title: Lest Must Be Followed by 'Should' or Bare Subjunctive
formula: Lest + Subject + SHOULD + V₁ | Lest + Subject + Bare V₁ [Strictly NO 'Not', NO 'May/Might/Will/Would']
ruleDescription:
**The 'Lest... Should' Conjunction Rule:**
1. **Lest** means 'for fear that' or 'so that... not' (ताकि ऐसा न हो जाए).
2. It is inherently negative, so you must **NEVER use 'not'** in the clause following lest.
3. The modal verb following 'lest' must strictly be **'SHOULD'** (or subjunctive bare verb V₁). Never use 'may', 'might', 'will', 'would', or 'shall'.
• Structure: `Walk carefully lest you should stumble.` (NOT 'lest you should not stumble' ❌).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Lest' (ताकि ऐसा न हो कि / कहीं ऐसा न हो जाए) के नियम:
1. 'Lest' के साथ सिर्फ और सिर्फ Modal Verb **'SHOULD'** (या base verb) का प्रयोग होता है ('May', 'Might', 'Will', 'Would' ❌ कभी नहीं आता)।
2. 'Lest' वाले भाग में कभी भी **'Not'** नहीं लगाया जाता (क्योंकि यह स्वयं नकारात्मक है)।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Imperative / Action + LEST + Subject + SHOULD + V₁`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Work hard lest you may fail' ❌ गलत है; 'Work hard lest you should fail' ✔ सही है।

title: Subject-Verb Agreement with 'As well as', 'Along with', 'Together with'
formula: Subject₁ + (as well as / along with / together with / with / in addition to / accompanied by / like / unlike / rather than / except / but / besides / and not) + Subject₂ ➔ Verb Agrees with SUBJECT 1
ruleDescription:
**First Subject Dominance Rule:**
When two subjects are joined by any of the following prepositions or connective phrases, the verb and possessive pronouns always agree strictly with the **FIRST SUBJECT**:
**Exhaustive List of Connectives:**
`As well as`, `Along with`, `Together with`, `With`, `In addition to`, `Accompanied by`, `Guided by`, `Headed by`, `Controlled by`, `Like`, `Unlike`, `Rather than`, `And not`, `Except`, `Besides`, `But`, `No less than`, `Including`, `Excluding`.
• Example: `The Captain (S₁), along with his sailors (S₂), was drowned.` (Singular verb 'was' agrees with 'Captain').
• Example: `The teachers (S₁), as well as the principal (S₂), have arrived.` (Plural verb 'have' agrees with 'teachers').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब दो Subjects इन शब्दों से जुड़े हों, तो Verb हमेशा **पहले Subject (Subject₁)** के अनुसार आती है।
**पूरी सूची**: As well as, Along with, Together with, With, In addition to, Accompanied by, Like, Unlike, Rather than, And not, Except, Besides, But, No less than.
**फॉर्मूला**: `Subject₁ + [Connective] + Subject₂ + Verb (according to Subject₁)`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'The father, along with his sons, are going' ❌ गलत है; 'The father, along with his sons, is going' ✔ सही है।

ruleDescription:

When two subjects are joined by correlative conjunctions, the verb and pronouns always agree with the **NEAREST SUBJECT** (the subject immediately adjacent to the verb):

ruleDescription:
**'Many a' vs 'Many' Structural Contrast:**
1. **'Many a' / 'Many an'** focuses on individual members one by one. It strictly takes a **Singular Noun** and a **Singular Verb**:
• `Many a soldier was decorated for bravery.`
• `Many an applicant has submitted the form.`
2. In contrast, **'Many'**, **'A great many'**, or **'A good many'** take a **Plural Noun** and a **Plural Verb**:
• `A great many soldiers were decorated.`

title: Nouns Not Taking Possessive Case (Separation, Mention, Report, Sight)
formula: Nouns that do NOT take Possessive ('s): Separation, Leave, Excuse, Mention, Report, Sight, Pardon, Favour
ruleDescription:
The following nouns never take an apostrophe possessive case (**'s**) with personal pronouns (your, his, my). Instead, use the preposition **'from / of'**:
**Exhaustive List of Words:**
1. **Separation** ➔ `Separation from you` (NOT 'Your separation' ❌)
2. **Leave** ➔ `Leave of him` (NOT 'His leave' ❌)
3. **Excuse** ➔ `Excuse from you` (NOT 'Your excuse' ❌)
4. **Mention** ➔ `Mention of you / him` (NOT 'Your mention' ❌)
5. **Report** ➔ `Report of him` (NOT 'His report' ❌)
6. **Sight** ➔ `At the sight of him` (NOT 'At his sight' ❌)
7. **Pardon** ➔ `Pardon from / of you` (NOT 'Your pardon' ❌)
8. **Favour** ➔ `A favour from / of you` (NOT 'Your favour' ❌).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: इन 8 संज्ञाओं के साथ कभी भी Possessive Case (My, Your, His + Noun) या Apostrophe ('s) का प्रयोग नहीं होता। इनके साथ 'Of / From' का प्रयोग होता है।
**पूरी सूची व सही रूप**:
1. **Your separation** ❌ ➔ `Separation from you` ✔ (आपसे जुदाई)
2. **At his sight** ❌ ➔ `At the sight of him` ✔ (उसको देखते ही)
3. **Your mention** ❌ ➔ `Mention of you` ✔ (आपका ज़िक्र)
4. **Do me your favour** ❌ ➔ `Do me a favour` ✔ (मुझ पर एक उपकार)
5. **His leave** ❌ ➔ `Leave of him` ✔ (उससे विदाई)
6. **Your pardon** ❌ ➔ `Pardon from you` ✔ (आपसे क्षमा).

title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Collective Nouns (Jury, Committee, Team)

ruleDescription:
**Collective Nouns Agreement (Jury, Committee, Team, Council, Audience):**
1. **United Action**: When the members act together as a single body with unanimous consent ➔ Takes **Singular Verb** and pronoun **'it / its'**:
• `The jury has given its verdict.`
• `The committee is unanimous in its decision.`
2. **Divided Action / Individual Focus**: When members have conflicting opinions or perform separate individual actions ➔ Takes **Plural Verb** and pronoun **'they / their'**:
• `The jury are divided in their opinions.`
• `The committee were taking their seats.`

title: Until (Time Limit) vs Unless (Conditional Prohibition)
formula: Until (Time Limit / 'Till that time') | Unless (Condition / 'If not') [NEVER use 'Not' or Future Tense inside clause]
ruleDescription:
**'Until' vs 'Unless' Core Distinctions:**
1. **Until** is **Time-oriented** (means 'up to the point in time that').
2. **Unless** is **Condition-oriented** (means 'except if' or 'if... not').
3. Both are inherently negative words, so **never use 'not' or 'never'** inside the clause introduced by until/unless.
4. Do not use future tense ('will/shall') in the until/unless clause.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Until' और 'Unless' का अंतर:
• **Until**: समय (Time) को दर्शाता है (जब तक कि... तब तक)।
• **Unless**: शर्त (Condition) को दर्शाता है (यदि नहीं / अगर ऐसा न हुआ तो)।
**दो महत्वपूर्ण नियम**:
1. इनके साथ कभी भी **'Not'** नहीं आता (क्योंकि ये स्वयं नकारात्मक हैं)।
2. इनके clause में 'will/shall' नहीं आता (Simple Present आता है)।
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Unless you do not work hard, you will fail' ❌ गलत है; 'Unless you work hard, you will fail' ✔ सही है।

title: Stative Verbs Not Used in Continuous/Progressive Tenses
formula: Stative Verbs (Perception, Emotion, Thinking, Possession) ➔ Simple Tenses ONLY [NO '-ing' Continuous Form]
ruleDescription:
**Stative Verbs (Non-Action Verbs):**
Stative verbs express a state or condition rather than a physical dynamic action. They are NOT used in progressive/continuous (-ing) tenses in standard English:
**Categorized Exhaustive List of Stative Verbs:**
1. **Verbs of Perception / Senses**: `See`, `Hear`, `Smell`, `Taste`, `Notice`, `Recognize`, `Feel`.
2. **Verbs of Thinking / Mental States**: `Know`, `Understand`, `Believe`, `Think`, `Remember`, `Forget`, `Doubt`, `Realize`, `Suppose`, `Agree`, `Mean`.

title: Subjunctive Mood & Unreal Past ('If I were you', 'I wish I had')
formula: Unreal Past / Subjunctive Mood: If + Subject + WERE (for all persons) | I wish + Subject + WERE / HAD V₃
ruleDescription:
**The Subjunctive Mood of Wish & Hypothesis:**
When expressing an imaginary situation, hypothetical wish, or impossible condition, the linking verb is ALWAYS **'WERE'** for all subjects (even with singular subjects like 'I', 'he', 'she', 'it'):
**Key Trigger Words:**
`If`, `As if`, `As though`, `I wish`, `Would that`, `Suppose`.
• `If I were a king, I would help the poor.` (NOT 'If I was a king' ❌)
• `He talks as if he were my boss.` (NOT 'as if he was' ❌)
• `I wish she were here today.` (NOT 'I wish she was' ❌).

**मुख्य नियम**: काल्पनिक वर्तमान (Hypothetical condition), इच्छा (Wish) या असम्भव शर्त में 'Be' क्रिया का रूप हमेशा **'WERE'** होता है (चाहे Subject Singular 'I/He/She' ही क्यों न हो; 'Was' ❌ कभी नहीं आता)।
**प्रमुख Triggers**: If, I wish, As if, As though, Would that, Supposing.
**फॉर्मूला**: `If + Subject + WERE + Complement, Subject + WOULD + V₁`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'If I was the Prime Minister' ❌ गलत है; 'If I were the Prime Minister' ✔ सही है।

title: Relative Pronoun Verb Agreement (It is I who am responsible)
formula: It is / was + Subject Pronoun + Relative Pronoun (Who/Which/That) + Verb (Agrees with ANTECEDENT)
ruleDescription:
**Relative Pronoun Antecedent Agreement Rule:**
In cleft sentences of the pattern **'It is [Subject] who...'**, the verb following the relative pronoun must strictly agree with the pronoun/noun immediately preceding it (its **Antecedent**):
• `It is I who AM to blame.` (Verb 'am' agrees with 'I', NOT 'is' ❌).
• `It is you who HAVE helped me.` (Verb 'have' agrees with 'you').
• `It is he who HAS completed the project.` (Verb 'has' agrees with 'he').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'It is / It was + Pronoun + Who...' वाले वाक्यों में Who के बाद आने वाली Verb अपने पूर्ववर्ती (Antecedent) Pronoun के Person और Number के अनुसार आती है।
**फॉर्मूला**: `It is + [I / You / He / We / They] + WHO + Verb (according to antecedent)`
• It is I who **am** (I के साथ 'am' आएगा, 'is' ❌ नहीं)
• It is you who **are** / **have**.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'It is I who is responsible for the error' ❌ गलत है; 'It is I who am responsible...' ✔ सही है।

title: Present Perfect Tense with 'Since + Simple Past Point in Time'
formula: Present Perfect (Has/Have + V₃) + SINCE + Simple Past (V₂ / Point in Time)
ruleDescription:
**'Since' as a Time Conjunction:**
When **'Since'** connects two clauses expressing that a state has continued from a specific past event up to the present:
1. The **Main Clause** (before 'since') must be in the **Present Perfect Tense (Has/Have + V₃)** or Present Perfect Continuous.
2. The **Subordinate Clause** (after 'since') must strictly be in the **Simple Past Tense (V₂)**.
• Structure: `[Present Perfect] + SINCE + [Simple Past (V₂)]`
• Example: `Five years have passed since my grandfather died.`
• Example: `I have not seen him since he left Mumbai.`
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब 'Since' दो वाक्यों को जोड़ता है (तब से लेकर अब तक के अर्थ में):
**1. मुख्य वाक्य (Since से पहले)**: `Present Perfect (Has/Have + V₃)`
**2. 'Since' के बाद वाला वाक्य**: `Simple Past (V₂)`
**फॉर्मूला**: `Subject + have/has + V₃ + SINCE + Subject + V₂`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Two years passed since he has joined' ❌ गलत है; 'Two years have passed since he joined' ✔ सही है।

title: 'Used to + V₁' (Past Habit) vs 'Be/Get Used to + Gerund' (Accustomed to)
formula: Used to + V₁ (Past Discontinued Habit) vs Be / Get used to + GERUND (V-ing) (Accustomed to)
ruleDescription:
**'Used to' Dual Construction Rule:**
1. **Past Discontinued Habit**: `Subject + USED TO + V₁` (expresses an action routinely done in the past that no longer occurs):
• `He used to smoke, but he quit last year.`
2. **Habituated / Accustomed**: `Subject + Be-verb (is/am/are/was/were) / Get + USED TO + Gerund (V-ing)` (expresses being accustomed to a current activity):
• `He is used to waking up early in the morning.`
• `She quickly got used to driving on the left.`
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Used to' की दो अलग-अलग व्याकरणिक संरचनाएं:
**1. भूतकाल की पुरानी आदत (Past Habit)**: `Subject + used to + V₁` (e.g. He used to play cricket - वह खेला करता था).
**2. अभ्यस्त होना (Accustomed to)**: `Subject + is/am/are/was/were + used to + Verb-ing` (e.g. He is used to working hard - वह कठिन परिश्रम करने का आदी है).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He is used to wake up early' ❌ गलत है; 'He is used to waking up early' ✔ सही है।

title: Nouns Plural in Form but Singular in Meaning (Physics, Mathematics, News, Innings)

ruleDescription:

1. **Subjects / Academic Disciplines**: `Physics`, `Mathematics`, `Economics`, `Ethics`, `Politics`, `Linguistics`, `Phonetics`, `Statistics`, `Civics`, `Mechanics`.

3. **Games & Sports**: `Billiards`, `Darts`, `Draughts`, `Bowls`, `Dominoes`, `Athletics`, `Gymnastics`.
4. **Miscellaneous**: `News`, `Innings`, `Series`, `Species`, `Summons` (Plural is 'Summonses').
**Special Exception**: When 'Mathematics', 'Statistics', or 'Politics' are preceded by a possessive adjective (e.g. 'My mathematics', 'His politics'), they refer to calculation ability or political views and take a **Plural Verb** (e.g., 'His mathematics are weak').

title: Nouns Singular in Form but Plural in Meaning (Cattle, Police, Poultry, Gentry)
formula: Nouns Singular in Form but Plural in Meaning + Plural Verb [Never add 's/es']
ruleDescription:
Certain collective nouns have no **'-s'** ending and look singular, but they are grammatically plural in nature and always take a **Plural Verb**. Never add 's' or 'es' to them:
**Exhaustive List:**
1. **Cattle** (NOT 'Cattles' ➔ Cattle are grazing)
2. **Police** (Police have caught the thief)
3. **Gentry** (High social class people ➔ Gentry were present)
4. **Poultry** (Poultry are kept for meat/eggs)
5. **Peasantry** (Small farmers ➔ Peasantry are suffering)
6. **Clergy** (Priests / Church ministers ➔ Clergy were invited)
7. **People / Folk** (People are demanding justice)
8. **Vermin** (Harmful pests/insects ➔ Vermin carry diseases)
9. **Infantry** (Foot soldiers ➔ Infantry are marching)
10. **Cavalry** (Horseback soldiers ➔ Cavalry were deployed)
11. **Artillery** (Heavy weapons army ➔ Artillery were positioned)
12. **Children** (Children are playing)
13. **Brethren** (Members of a community ➔ Brethren are united).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: ये Nouns रूप में Singular दिखते हैं, लेकिन अर्थ में हमेशा **Plural** होते हैं। इनके साथ **Plural Verb** आती है और इनमें कभी भी 's/es' (जैसे Cattles ❌, Polices ❌) नहीं लगाया जाता।
**पूरी सूची**: Cattle, Police, Gentry (कुलीन वर्ग), Poultry, Peasantry (किसान वर्ग), Clergy (पादरी वर्ग), Folk, Vermin (कीड़े-मकोड़े), Infantry (पैदल सेना), Cavalry (घुड़सवार सेना).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'The cattles are grazing in the field' ❌ गलत है; 'The cattle are grazing in the field' ✔ सही है।

title: Uncountable Nouns Not Taking Plural 's' or A/An (Furniture, Luggage, Advice, Information)
formula: Uncountable Nouns ➔ NO Plural 's/es' + NO 'A/An' + Singular Verb
ruleDescription:
The following nouns are strictly **Uncountable**. They never take a plural 's' or 'es', never take articles 'a' or 'an', and always take a **Singular Verb**:
**Exhaustive List of Uncountable Nouns:**
`Furniture`, `Luggage`, `Baggage`, `Scenery`, `Poetry`, `Machinery`, `Information`, `Advice`, `Work`, `Evidence`, `Stationery`, `Cutlery`, `Crockery`, `Jewellery`, `Alphabet`, `Percentage`, `Hair`, `Bread`, `Soap`, `Confectionery`, `Mischief`, `Cost`, `Fuel`, `Paper`.
**Countable Unit Phrases to Count Them:**
• 'A piece of furniture' / 'Items of furniture'
• 'A piece of information' / 'Pieces of information'
• 'A word of advice' / 'Words of advice'
• 'A loaf of bread' / 'Loaves of bread'
• 'A bar of soap' / 'Bars of soap'
• 'A strand of hair' / 'Strands of hair'.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: ये सभी Nouns Uncountable होते हैं। इनके साथ कभी भी 's/es' नहीं लगाया जाता (जैसे Furnitures ❌, Sceneries ❌, Informations ❌), न ही इनसे पहले 'a/an' आता है।
**पूरी सूची**: Furniture, Luggage, Baggage, Scenery, Poetry, Machinery, Information, Advice, Work, Evidence, Stationery, Jewellery, Alphabet, Bread, Soap, Hair.
**गिनने का सही तरीका**: 'A piece of information', 'Pieces of advice', 'Loaves of bread'.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'The sceneries of Kashmir are beautiful' ❌ गलत है; 'The scenery of Kashmir is beautiful' ✔ सही है।

title: Conjunction Pairings: 'Between... And' vs 'From... To'

ruleDescription:
**Fixed Correlative Preposition Pairs:**
1. **Between** is always paired with **'AND'** (e.g. 'Between 10 AM and 5 PM').
2. **From** is always paired with **'TO'** (e.g. 'From 10 AM to 5 PM').
3. Never mix pairs: 'Between 10 AM to 5 PM' ❌ is a widespread grammatical error.
4. Avoid 'Between each / every' (e.g. 'There is a break between each period' ➔ 'Between the periods' ).

title: Order of Multiple Adjectives Before a Noun (OSASCOMP Rule)
formula: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material -> Purpose + Noun
ruleDescription:
When multiple adjectives qualify a single noun, they must follow the **OSASCOMP** order:
1. **O**pinion (beautiful, lovely)
2. **S**ize (big, tiny)
3. **A**ge (old, young, antique)
4. **S**hape (round, square)
5. **C**olor (red, black)
6. **O**rigin (Indian, French)
7. **M**aterial (wooden, metallic)
8. **P**urpose (wedding, sleeping) + Noun.

क्रम: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material -> Purpose.
परीक्षा टिप: 'a black handsome young man' गलत है; 'a handsome young black man' सही है।

title: Superfluous Expressions Avoidance (Return back, Cousin brother, Blunder mistake)
formula: Eliminate Superfluous / Redundant Words (Do NOT Repeat Same Meaning in Pair)
ruleDescription:
In English, superfluous (redundant) expressions violate grammatical economy and are heavily tested in SSC examinations:
**Master Table of Superfluous Traps:**
1. `Return back` ➔ **Return** ✔
2. `Revert back` ➔ **Revert** ✔
3. `Cousin brother / sister` ➔ **Cousin** ✔
4. `Blunder mistake / Big blunder` ➔ **Blunder** ✔
5. `Kindly request` ➔ **Request** ✔
6. `Flee away` ➔ **Flee** ✔
7. `Repeat again` ➔ **Repeat** ✔
8. `Recall back` ➔ **Recall** ✔
9. `Withdraw back` ➔ **Withdraw** ✔
10. `Reason why... because` ➔ **The reason is that...** ✔
11. `Equally as good as` ➔ **As good as / Equally good** ✔
12. `Passing marks` ➔ **Pass marks** ✔
13. `Family members` ➔ **Members of the family** ✔
14. `Link language` ➔ **Common language** ✔
15. `Proudy` ➔ **Proud** ✔
16. `Supposing if` ➔ **Supposing / If** ✔.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Superfluous (अनावश्यक/दोहराव वाले) शब्दों का प्रयोग वर्जित है। जब एक शब्द में ही अर्थ समाहित हो, तो उसके साथ अतिरिक्त शब्द न जोड़ें।
**प्रमुख SSC एरर जोड़े**:
• Return back ❌ ➔ Return ✔
• Cousin brother ❌ ➔ Cousin ✔
• Big blunder ❌ ➔ Blunder ✔
• Flee away ❌ ➔ Flee ✔
• Passing marks ❌ ➔ Pass marks ✔
• Revert back ❌ ➔ Revert ✔
• Repeat again ❌ ➔ Repeat ✔.

ruleDescription:
**'Beside' vs 'Besides' Distinction:**
1. **Beside** (without 's') means 'at the side of' or 'adjacent to' (physical location).
• Example: `She came and sat beside me.`
2. **Besides** (with 's') means 'in addition to' or 'as well as' / 'apart from'.
• Example: `Besides English, he speaks fluent French and German.`

title: 'Prefer... To' / 'Prefer V-ing to V-ing' (Never 'Prefer Than')
formula: Prefer Noun/V-ing + TO + Noun/V-ing | Preferable + TO [Never 'Prefer... than' ❌]
ruleDescription:
**The 'Prefer' Grammar Construction:**
1. The verb **'Prefer'** and adjective **'Preferable'** take the preposition **'TO'**, NEVER 'than'.
2. Structure with nouns: `Subject + prefer + Noun + TO + Noun` (e.g. 'I prefer tea to coffee').
3. Structure with actions: `Subject + prefer + Gerund (V-ing) + TO + Gerund (V-ing)` (e.g. 'I prefer reading to writing').
4. Structure with infinitives: When comparing two infinitives, use 'rather than' (e.g. 'I prefer to read rather than write').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Prefer' और 'Preferable' के बाद तुलना के लिए हमेशा **'TO'** आता है ('Than' ❌ कभी नहीं आता)।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Subject + prefer + [Noun/V-ing] + TO + [Noun/V-ing]`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'I prefer milk than tea' ❌ गलत है; 'I prefer milk to tea' ✔ सही है।

title: Question Tags Rules & Agreement (Positive Statement -> Negative Tag)
formula: Positive Statement ➔ Negative Tag | Negative Statement ➔ Positive Tag | 'I am' ➔ 'Aren't I?' | 'Let's' ➔ 'Shall we?'
ruleDescription:
**Question Tag Master Rules:**
1. **Tense Agreement**: The tag must always match the tense of the main clause.
2. **Polarity Inversion**: Positive sentence ➔ Negative tag (`isn't he?`); Negative sentence ➔ Positive tag (`is he?`).
3. **Subject Pronoun**: The subject in the tag is always a **Personal Pronoun** (never a noun).
4. **Key Special Tag Traps:**
• `I am a teacher` ➔ `Aren't I?` (NOT 'Amn't I' ❌)
• `Let's go for a walk` ➔ `Shall we?`
• `Open the door` (Imperative) ➔ `Will you?` / `Won't you?`
• `Nobody came` (Negative subject) ➔ `Did they?`
• `Each / Everyone is happy` ➔ `Aren't they?` (They takes plural verb 'aren't').
• Sentences with `Seldom`, `Hardly`, `Scarcely`, `Few`, `Little` are already negative ➔ Positive tag (`does he?`).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Question Tag के प्रमुख नियम:
1. सकारात्मक वाक्य ➔ नकारात्मक Tag (He is honest, isn't he?).
2. नकारात्मक वाक्य ➔ सकारात्मक Tag (He is not honest, is he?).
**SSC के महत्वपूर्ण स्पेशल Tags**:
• 'I am fine' ➔ `Aren't I?` (Amn't I ❌ कभी नहीं होता).
• 'Let's start' ➔ `Shall we?`
• 'Hardly/Seldom' वाले वाक्य नकारात्मक माने जाते हैं ➔ Positive Tag (e.g., He seldom comes, does he?).
• 'Everyone / Somebody' के लिए Tag में Pronoun **'They'** आता है (e.g., Everyone is ready, aren't they?).

title: Singular Noun + Preposition + Singular Noun Structure (Page after page, Row upon row)
formula: Singular Noun + Preposition + Same Singular Noun [Both Nouns strictly Singular + Singular Verb]
ruleDescription:
**Repeated Noun Preposition Construction:**
When the same noun is repeated before and after a preposition, both nouns must strictly be in the **Singular Form**, and the sentence takes a **Singular Verb**:
**Exhaustive List:**
• `Page after page` (NOT 'Pages after pages' ❌)
• `Door to door` (NOT 'Doors to doors' ❌)
• `Row upon row` (NOT 'Rows upon rows' ❌)
• `Day by day` (NOT 'Days by days' ❌)
• `Ship after ship` (NOT 'Ships after ships' ❌)
• `Town after town` (NOT 'Towns after towns' ❌)
• `Word for word` (NOT 'Words for words' ❌).
• Example: `Page after page of the holy book was read.` (Singular verb 'was').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब Preposition के दोनों तरफ एक ही Noun दोहराया जाए, तो दोनों Nouns अनिवार्य रूप से **Singular** होंगे और Verb भी **Singular** ही आएगी।
**पूरी सूची**:
• Page after page (Pages after pages ❌ गलत)
• Door to door (Doors to doors ❌ गलत)
• Row upon row (Rows upon rows ❌ गलत)
• Day by day, Town after town, Word for word.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Pages after pages were read' ❌ गलत है; 'Page after page was read' ✔ सही है।

title: 'The + Adjective' Expressing Whole Class of People (The rich are, The poor are)
formula: The + Adjective (Representing Whole Class of People) + Plural Verb [Never add 's/es' to adjective]
ruleDescription:
**'The + Adjective' Plural Class Rule:**
When the definite article **'The'** is placed before certain qualitative adjectives, it converts the adjective into a plural noun representing the entire class of such people. It takes a **Plural Verb**, and you must NEVER add 's' or 'es' to the adjective:
**Exhaustive List:**
• `The rich` = Rich people (NOT 'The riches' ❌)
• `The poor` = Poor people (NOT 'The poors' ❌)
• `The blind` = Blind people (NOT 'The blinds' ❌)
• `The deaf` = Deaf people
• `The dumb` = Dumb people
• `The honest` = Honest people
• `The needy` = Needy people
• `The elderly` = Elderly people
• `The brave` = Brave people.
• Example: `The poor are often honest and hardworking.` (Plural verb 'are').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब किसी Adjective के पहले 'The' लगा दिया जाता है, तो वह उस पूरे वर्ग/समुदाय के लोगों को दर्शाता है और हमेशा **Plural Noun** बन जाता है। इसके साथ **Plural Verb** आती है और इसमें कभी भी 's/es' नहीं लगाया जाता।
**पूरी सूची**: The rich (अमीर लोग), The poor (गरीब लोग - 'The poors' ❌ गलत), The blind (अंधे लोग), The honest (ईमानदार लोग).
**फॉर्मूला**: `The + Adjective + Plural Verb (are / were / have)`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'The poors are suffering' ❌ गलत है; 'The poor are suffering' ✔ सही है।

title: Demonstrative Pronouns in Comparison: 'That of' (Singular) vs 'Those of' (Plural)
formula: Singular Comparison ➔ 'That of' | Plural Comparison ➔ 'Those of' [Avoid False Comparisons]
ruleDescription:
**Rule of Logical Comparison ('That of' & 'Those of'):**
Comparison must always be made between equal/similar entities. When comparing qualities or features of two items:
1. Use **'that of'** to replace a Singular Noun.
• `The climate of Delhi is hotter than that of Mumbai.` (NOT 'hotter than Mumbai' ❌).
2. Use **'those of'** to replace a Plural Noun.
• `The streets of London are cleaner than those of New York.` (NOT 'cleaner than New York' ❌).

**1. Singular Noun के लिए**: 'Than' के बाद **'that of'** का प्रयोग करें (जैसे 'The climate of Delhi is hotter than that of Mumbai').
**2. Plural Noun के लिए**: 'Than' के बाद **'those of'** का प्रयोग करें (जैसे 'The roads of India are wider than those of Nepal').
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'My shoes are better than you' ❌ (मेरे जूते तुमसे बेहतर हैं - गलत); सही 'My shoes are better than yours / those of you' ✔ होगा।

title: Preposition Before Relative Pronouns (To whom, With which, In which)

ruleDescription: When a preposition is placed directly before a relative pronoun, use **'whom'** for persons (e.g., 'to whom', 'with whom') and **'which'** for things (e.g., 'in which', 'for which'). Prepositions are never placed directly before 'who' or 'that'.

title: 'Doubt / Doubtful': 'If / Whether' in Affirmative vs 'That' in Negative / Interrogative
formula: Doubt / Doubtful in Affirmative -> If / Whether | Doubt / Doubtful in Negative / Interrogative -> That
ruleDescription:
- In **Affirmative sentences** (where uncertainty exists), use **'if'** or **'whether'** after 'doubt' or 'doubtful'.
- In **Negative and Interrogative sentences** (where uncertainty is removed), use **'that'** after 'doubt' or 'doubtful'.
hindiExplanation:
Affirmative (सकारात्मक) वाक्यों में Doubt/Doubtful के बाद 'If' या 'Whether' का प्रयोग होता है।
Negative (नकारात्मक) या Interrogative (प्रश्नवाचक) वाक्यों में Doubt/Doubtful के बाद हमेशा 'That' का प्रयोग होता है।
परीक्षा टिप: 'He does not doubt if they will win' गलत है; 'He does not doubt that they will win' सही है।

title: Avoidance of Split Infinitives (To + Adverb + V₁ ❌ -> To + V₁ + Adverb)
formula: To + V₁ + Adverb (or Adverb + To + V₁) [Never insert adverb between 'to' and V₁]
ruleDescription: An infinitive is composed of **'to + V₁'**. In formal English and standard competitive exams, avoid inserting an adverb between 'to' and the verb base form (known as a **Split Infinitive**). Place the adverb either after the verb or before 'to'.
hindiExplanation:

title: Verbs Taking Direct Prepositions (Prohibit from, Prevent from, Abstain from, Refrain from)
formula: Verbs with Fixed Preposition + Gerund (V-ing) [From / On / Of / In]
ruleDescription:
The following verbs strictly govern specific prepositions followed by a **Gerund (V-ing)**:
**1. Verbs Taking 'FROM + V-ing':**
`Prohibit`, `Prevent`, `Abstain`, `Refrain`, `Debar`, `Desist`, `Deter`, `Disqualify`, `Protect`, `Escape` + FROM + V-ing.
**2. Verbs Taking 'ON + V-ing':**
`Insist`, `Persist`, `Depend`, `Rely`, `Congratulate`, `Compliment` + ON + V-ing.
**3. Adjectives Taking 'OF + Noun/V-ing':**
`Fond`, `Afraid`, `Aware`, `Beware`, `Conscious`, `Guilty`, `Jealous`, `Short`, `Tired`, `Worthy`, `Capable`, `Desirous` + OF.
**4. Verbs Taking 'IN + V-ing':**
`Succeed`, `Excel`, `Persist`, `Interested`, `Indulge` + IN + V-ing.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: इन विशिष्ट Verbs और Adjectives के साथ Fixed Prepositions और Gerund (V-ing) का ही प्रयोग होता है।
**पूरी सूची**:
• **FROM + V-ing**: Prohibit, Prevent, Abstain, Refrain, Debar, Desist, Deter, Disqualify.
• **ON + V-ing**: Insist on, Persist on, Congratulate on, Compliment on.
• **OF**: Fond of, Afraid of, Aware of, Beware of, Guilty of, Capable of.
• **IN + V-ing**: Succeed in, Excel in, Interested in.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He prevented me to go there' ❌ गलत है; 'He prevented me from going there' ✔ सही है।

formula: An + Vowel Sound (अ, आ, इ, ई, ए, ऐ, ओ, औ) | A + Consonant Sound (क, ख, ग, य, व...)
ruleDescription:
The choice between indefinite articles **'a'** and **'an'** is governed strictly by the **initial pronunciation sound**, NOT by the spelling letter.
- Use **'An'** before words starting with a vowel sound (e.g., an honest man, an MBA, an hour, an heir).

title: Transitive Verbs Taking Direct Objects Without Preposition (Discuss, Describe, Reach, Order, Attack)

ruleDescription:
The following transitive verbs directly take their object without any preposition. Adding a preposition after them is a severe grammatical error:
**Complete List of Zero-Preposition Verbs:**

title: Pronoun Order Rule: 231 for Good Acts (2nd, 3rd, 1st Person) vs 123 for Mistakes / Plurals
formula: Pronoun Order: 231 (Normal / Positive Actions) vs 123 (Negative / Blame / Mistakes / Plural Pronouns)
ruleDescription:
When multiple personal pronouns of different persons are used together joined by 'and', their order depends on the nature of the action:
**1. Normal / Good / Polite Actions ➔ Order 231:**
`2nd Person (You) ➔ 3rd Person (He/She/They) ➔ 1st Person (I/We)`
• Example: `You, he and I are going to attend the lecture.`
• Example: `You and he should complete the assignment.` (23)
• Example: `You and I have won the championship.` (21)
• Example: `He and I will manage the event.` (31)
**2. Confession of Mistake, Guilt, Blame, Crime or Plural Pronouns ➔ Order 123:**
`1st Person (I/We) ➔ 2nd Person (You) ➔ 3rd Person (He/She/They)`
• Example: `I, you and he made the mistake.`
• Example: `We, you and they are responsible for the failure.`
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: जब एक ही वाक्य में तीनों Persons के Pronouns एक साथ आएं, तो उनका क्रम नियम:
**1. सामान्य / अच्छे कार्यों में (231 Rule)**: 2nd Person ➔ 3rd Person ➔ 1st Person (You, he and I).
**2. भूल / गलती / अपराध स्वीकार करने में (123 Rule)**: 1st Person ➔ 2nd Person ➔ 3rd Person (I, you and he).
**3. सभी Pronouns Plural होने पर (123 Rule)**: We, you and they.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'I, you and he will study together' ❌ गलत है; सही 'You, he and I will study together' ✔ होगा।

title: 'In Spite Of' = 'Despite' (Never use 'Despite Of')

ruleDescription:
**'Despite' vs 'In Spite Of' Distinction:**
1. **'In spite of'** is a 3-word phrase requiring the preposition 'of'.
2. **'Despite'** is a single preposition meaning the exact same thing, but it NEVER takes 'of'.
3. 'Despite of' ❌ is one of the most frequent error traps in SSC exams.
hindiExplanation:

• **Despite**: इसके साथ 'of' ❌ **कभी नहीं** आता।
**फॉर्मूला**: `Despite + Noun / V-ing` = `In spite of + Noun / V-ing`
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'Despite of hard work, he failed' ❌ गलत है; 'Despite hard work, he failed' ✔ सही है।

title: 'Comprise' = 'Consist Of' (Never use 'Comprise Of' in Active Voice)
formula: Comprise (Active Voice) = Consist of [NEVER use 'Comprise of' in Active Voice ❌]
ruleDescription:
**'Comprise' vs 'Consist of' Rule:**
1. **'Consist'** always takes the preposition **'of'** ('The book consists of 10 chapters').
2. **'Comprise'** means 'to consist of' or 'to be composed of'. In the **Active Voice, 'comprise' NEVER takes 'of'** ('The book comprises 10 chapters').
3. In the **Passive Voice**, 'be comprised of' is grammatically acceptable (e.g. 'The committee is comprised of 5 members').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Comprise' का अर्थ ही 'Consist of' (से मिलकर बना होना) होता है।
• **Active Voice में**: Comprise के साथ 'of' ❌ कभी नहीं आता (e.g., The team comprises 11 players).
• **Consist**: इसके साथ 'of' हमेशा आता है (The team consists of 11 players).
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'The committee comprises of ten members' ❌ गलत है; 'The committee comprises ten members' ✔ सही है।

title: 'Little', 'A Little', 'The Little' (Quantity) Distinctions
formula: Little (Almost None - Negative) | A Little (Some Quantity - Positive) | The Little (All that is available - Definite)
ruleDescription:
**Degrees of Uncountable Quantity (Little / A Little / The Little):**
1. **Little** (without article) = Hardly any / almost none. Has a negative meaning ('He has little hope of recovery' = almost no hope).
2. **A Little** = A small quantity / some amount. Has a positive meaning ('He has a little hope' = at least some hope exists).
3. **The Little** = The specific small amount that exists ('He spent the little money he had' = all of that small amount).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Uncountable Nouns की मात्रा दर्शाने के लिए:
• **Little** (न के बराबर - नकारात्मक अर्थ): 'There is little water in the jug' (लगभग खाली).
• **A Little** (थोड़ा/कुछ - सकारात्मक अर्थ): 'A little knowledge is a dangerous thing'.
• **The Little** (जो थोड़ा-बहुत सब का सब): 'He drank the little milk in the cup'.
**परीक्षा टिप**: यदि अर्थ सकारात्मक हो तो 'A little' लगाएं, यदि न के बराबर हो तो 'Little' लगाएं।

title: 'Few', 'A Few', 'The Few' (Number) Distinctions
formula: Few (Almost None - Negative) | A Few (Some Number - Positive) | The Few (All of that small number - Definite)
ruleDescription:
**Degrees of Countable Number (Few / A Few / The Few):**
1. **Few** (without article) = Almost none / negligible number (Negative meaning: 'Few people attended the seminar' = almost nobody).
2. **A Few** = Some number / a small number (Positive meaning: 'A few friends helped him' = at least some friends).
3. **The Few** = The specific small number of people/items that exist ('The few books he had were stolen').
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: Countable Nouns की संख्या दर्शाने के लिए:
• **Few** (न के बराबर - नकारात्मक अर्थ): 'Few students passed the exam' (लगभग कोई नहीं).
• **A Few** (कुछ/थोड़े - सकारात्मक अर्थ): 'A few students passed the exam' (कुछ छात्र पास हुए).
• **The Few** (जो कुछ थोड़े-बहुत थे वे सभी): 'The few clothes he had were burnt'.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'I have few friends, so I am very happy' ❌ गलत है; 'I have a few friends' ✔ सही है।

title: Absolute Adjectives Not Admitting Comparison (Unique, Perfect, Round, Supreme, Dead, Impossible)
formula: Absolute / Non-Gradable Adjectives ➔ NO 'More', NO 'Most', NO 'Very', NO 'Comparative / Superlative'
ruleDescription:
The following adjectives represent an absolute (highest / complete) state. They cannot be graded or compared. Therefore, words like 'more', 'most', 'very', 'comparatively' are never used before them:
**Complete List of Absolute Adjectives:**
1. **Unique** (NOT 'more unique' ❌ or 'most unique' ❌)
2. **Perfect** (NOT 'most perfect' ❌)
3. **Universal** (NOT 'more universal' ❌)
4. **Complete** (NOT 'more complete' ❌)
5. **Dead** (NOT 'more dead' ❌)
6. **Impossible** (NOT 'most impossible' ❌)
7. **Eternal** (NOT 'more eternal' ❌)
8. **Infinite** (NOT 'more infinite' ❌)
9. **Supreme** (NOT 'most supreme' ❌)
10. **Absolute** (NOT 'more absolute' ❌)
11. **Chief / Principal** (NOT 'most chief' ❌)
12. **Round / Circular / Square / Triangular** (Geometric shapes)
13. **Entire / Whole** (NOT 'more entire' ❌)
14. **Flawless / Matchless / Peerless** (NOT 'more flawless' ❌).
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: ये Absolute Adjectives (पूर्ण अवस्था वाले विशेषण) होते हैं। इनमें कोई तुलना या मात्रा (Degrees of Comparison) नहीं हो सकती। इनके पहले 'More', 'Most', 'Very' लगाना पूर्णतः वर्जित है।
**पूरी सूची**: Unique, Perfect, Universal, Complete, Dead, Impossible, Eternal, Infinite, Supreme, Absolute, Round, Square, Entire, Flawless, Matchless.
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'This is the most unique idea' ❌ गलत है; 'This is a unique idea' ✔ सही है।

title: Adverb 'Enough' Follows the Adjective It Modifies (Smart enough, not 'enough smart')
formula: Adjective / Adverb + ENOUGH (Positive Degree) vs ENOUGH + Noun
ruleDescription:
**Position of 'Enough' in English Grammar:**
1. When **'Enough'** modifies an **Adjective or Adverb**, it is always placed **AFTER** the adjective/adverb, and the adjective must be in the **Positive Degree** (NOT comparative):
• `Fast enough` (NOT 'enough fast' ❌)
• `Wise enough` (NOT 'wiser enough' ❌ or 'enough wise' ❌)
• `Strong enough` (NOT 'stronger enough' ❌).
2. When **'Enough'** functions as an adjective modifying a **Noun**, it is placed **BEFORE** the noun:
• `Enough money` (NOT 'money enough' ❌)
• `Enough time`.
hindiExplanation:
**मुख्य नियम**: 'Enough' का स्थान:
**1. Adjective या Adverb के साथ**: 'Enough' हमेशा Adjective के **बाद** आता है और Adjective हमेशा **Positive Degree** में रहता है (e.g. 'He is smart enough', 'enough smart' ❌ नहीं).
**2. Noun के साथ**: 'Enough' हमेशा Noun से **पहले** आता है (e.g. 'He has enough money').
**परीक्षा टिप**: 'He is enough rich to buy a car' ❌ गलत है; सही 'He is rich enough to buy a car' ✔ होगा।
